basis: TCA-cycle disorder defined by severe neurodevelopmental impairment and cerebral malformations; hepatic failure/cholestasis in 2/2 selected cases does not establish typical prevalence.

decisions.hepatic: none: hepatic failure/cholestasis in 2/2 selected cases is insufficient to establish >=30% across this predominantly neurologic disease.
decisions.neurologic: primary: psychomotor impairment, seizures and cerebral malformations define the disease; encephalopathy is frequent (30-79%).

basis: Defining bifid nose, anorectal defects and renal malformations; renal agenesis in 6/9. Ebstein anomaly in 1/2 selected cases does not establish common cardiac involvement.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: Ebstein anomaly in 1/2 selected cases lacks sufficient evidence of >=30% prevalence across BNAR syndrome.

basis: Corticospinal degeneration defines disease; structural pes cavus/amyotrophy occur in 30-79%, and bladder sphincter dysfunction in 11/27. Isolated ocular reports lack established association.

decisions.renal: involved: bladder sphincter dysfunction in 11/27 (~41%) represents sustained urinary functional loss, beyond urgency alone.

basis: Benign dermal histiocytic tumor; ocular and other extracutaneous involvement occur in fewer than 30%. Dermal histiocytes alone do not establish blood or marrow disease.

decisions.haematologic: none: the defined lesion is a dermal histiocytic tumor without defining blood-cell, marrow or coagulation dysfunction.

basis: Intellectual disability and areflexia, genu valgum and small teeth are defining features; genu valgum occurs in 80-99% and microdontia in 30-79%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: small teeth are explicitly part of the syndrome's definition; microdontia occurs in 30-79%, and teeth belong to this axis.

basis: Photosensitive brittle-hair disorder; intellectual disability 3/3, cataracts 2/3, hearing impairment 1/3. Singleton immune and GI findings have weaker support and are omitted at the cap.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: immune abnormalities and recurrent infections have singleton evidence (1/1), weaker than the retained manifestations under the four-axis cap.
decisions.otologic: involved: hearing impairment in 1/3 (~33%) meets the threshold for functional damage, although the sample is very small.

basis: Osteosclerotic skeletal dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia and pulmonic stenosis each occur in 30-79%. Thick skin and hypertrichosis lack demonstrated functional damage.

decisions.dermatologic: none: thickened skin and hypertrichosis occur in 30-79%, but neither establishes destructive skin pathology or functional loss.

basis: Skin aplasia and intestinal lymphangiectasia; calvarial defects 80-99%, lymphopenia 30-79%. Hypogammaglobulinemia (30-79%) omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.haematologic: involved: persistent enteric lymphocyte loss causes lymphopenia in 30-79% and is explicitly described in the syndrome definition.
decisions.infectious_immune: none: antibody loss occurs in 30-79%, but ranks below frequent calvarial defects and defining lymphopenia under the four-axis cap.

basis: Bacillus anthracis infection; cutaneous ulcerative disease accounts for about 95% of naturally acquired cases. Pulmonary and gastrointestinal forms are minority subtypes.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: skin is a defined infection site and cutaneous disease accounts for about 95% of naturally acquired anthrax, supporting the umbrella label.

basis: Peripheral neuropathy, parkinsonism and ptosis define syndrome; chronic distal muscle wasting and foot deformity affect most (>50%) patients with typical CMT. Subtype-specific data are sparse.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: chronic denervation atrophy and structural foot deformities affect most (>50%) patients with CMT; this subtype's frequency is undocumented.
